title: TaGNN: An Efficient Topology-aware Accelerator for High-performance Dynamic Graph Neural Network
problem: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) suffer from low data parallelism due to snapshot-by-snapshot execution, creating memory contention from irregular vertex feature accesses and strict temporal dependencies.
motivation: DGNNs combine GNNs and RNNs for temporal graph analysis, but sequential snapshot execution severely limits parallelism and efficiency compared to static graph methods.
method: TaGNN speeds up dynamic graph neural networks by running multiple computations at the same time based on the graph's structure. Instead of recalculating everything each time step, it updates only the vertices (nodes) that actually change, while loading the unchanged ones just once per layer. The data is organized by the graph's topology and timestamps so the computer's fast memory cache works efficiently. When the RNN (recurrent neural network, which processes sequences) outputs are nearly identical between steps, it skips those redundant calculations.
key_novelty: TaGNN speeds up dynamic graph neural networks on FPGA by using the graph's structure to run multiple computations at once, organize data efficiently for the memory cache, and skip redundant neural network steps when outputs barely change.
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. FPGA-specific design; portability to other platforms not addressed.
primary_theme: FPGA acceleration for dynamic graph neural networks
